item.title: Government Lending 2.0: Putting a Price on Policy Risk
item.description: As federal credit becomes increasingly utilized, federal agencies need a framework to quantify policy risk and create a common language to balance strategic priorities with financial risks.

item.title: Does the Space Commerce Certification Create or Reduce Red Tape?
item.description: A new space mission certification aims to streamline U.S. regulatory processes and reduce uncertainty for space companies, but it may end up doing the opposite.

item.title: New Approaches to Address the Role of Gold in Sudan’s Civil War
item.description: Revenues from gold are a key driver of the conflict in Sudan. Recent EU sanctions are a start, but much more needs to be done to ensure the gold trade no longer finances bloodshed in the world’s most abandoned humanitarian crisis.

item.title: Proving Ground: China’s Strategic Ratcheting of the Philippines and the Indo-Pacific’s Gray Zone Problem
item.description: China’s maritime gray zone operations in the West Philippine Sea are the “tip of the spear” for China’s pressure campaign against the Philippines. It is essential that policymakers do not lose sight of the rest of the spear.

item.title: China’s Hunger Games
item.description: CSIS's Caitlin Welsh and Brian Hart analyze China's leveraging of food markets for geopolitical influence for Foreign Affairs.

item.title: What Happens if Congress Codifies Russia Sanctions?
item.description: The Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026 would codify roughly 6,800 designations and create a new tariff authority aimed at the largest buyers of Russian energy. Whether it produces real pressure on Moscow depends on executive branch implementation.
